Obsessed Pretenders fan bombarded singer Chrissie Hynde with 'deeply disturbing' messages that left her feeling 'physically sick', court hears

By ARTHUR PARASHAR, SPECIAL CORRESPONDENT

Published: 15:54 GMT, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:54 GMT, 18 November 2026

Add us as a preferred source

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:52
Instaread

An obsessed Pretenders fan bombarded singer Chrissie Hynde with 'deeply disturbing' messages that left her feeling 'physically sick', a court has heard. 

Bruce Krom, 50, allegedly spent two years 'bombarding' the Pretenders star's agency with written and voice messages, and sent gifts such as jewellery and a bonsai tree, between May 2024 and May 2026.

The two-year stalking campaign left the 75-year-old rock star fearing for the safety of her children and grandchildren, Southwark Crown Court heard.

1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE

In one message read out to the court, Krom said: 'She is the most beautiful princess in the world with a heart of gold.

'I would gladly meet her with security. I just want to finally meet her as a human being. She can stop by my flat any time, lunch or dinner on me.'

Jurors were told Krom, a former Domino's Pizza worker with joint US and UK nationality, has been deemed unfit to stand trial so they will have to determine whether he did the acts alleged, namely stalking of the star.

Ms Hynde was initially shielded from the allegations but was told in May 2026 after her team made a police report, jurors heard.

In a statement read out by the prosecution in court, Ms Hynde said: 'I have been deeply shocked and immediately concerned for my personal safety. I am taking these threats extremely seriously.'

She said she had previously been the victim of stalking in the US.

'It was an extremely stressful and frightening experience,' the singer songwriter continued.

Singer Chrissie Hynde (pictured) has said messages from an 'obsessed' fan accused of stalking her made her feel 'physically sick'

'These recent events have brought back many of those fears and anxiety.'

She said her profession requires her to maintain a public profile.

'The knowledge that an individual who appears fixated with me may be using these appearances to locate me is extremely unsettling and frightening,' she said.

'Knowing that this individual has apparently relocated himself to the city where I live has increased my vulnerability and fear for my personal safety.

'The impact that this has had on me personally has been substantial. I have seen the messages, I find them deeply disturbing.

'Reading them has made me feel physically sick and extremely distressed.'

Krom started posting on Facebook and Instagram about Ms Hynde in July 2024 before he began emailing and calling her London-based agency, Quietus, the court heard.

He left at least 14.5 hours of 'long, rambling messages', prosecutor Charles Ward-Jackson told jurors.

'They contained expressions of admiration for Ms Hynde, a desire to meet her… but also a slightly disturbing and obsessive interest in her,' Mr Ward-Jackson said.

He would express feelings of romantic love and talk to her about personal issues such as his cat and his mother, the court heard.

He claims to have seen her once in Barkers department store in Kensington in the mid-1990s and 'since then seems to have nursed an obsessive memory of that encounter', the prosecutor said.

'He spent two years bombarding her agency with written and voice messages which the Crown say amounts to stalking, causing serious alarm and distress,' Mr Ward-Jackson said.

'It all came to an end when Mr Krom was arrested on 15 May 2026.

Bruce Krom (pictured), 50, allegedly spent two years 'bombarding' the Pretenders star's agency with written and voice messages, and sent gifts such as jewellery and a bonsai tree, between May 2024 and May 2026

'The essence of it is he contacted her on multiple occasions by various means, that's what this case is about.

'He bombarded the agency with written messages, and oral messages...and on one occasion said he would actually turn up and meet Ms Hynde at a London recording studio in Maida Vale.'

Krom sent the singer a golden necklace during the Christmas period in 2024 and gifts around Valentine's Day in 2025 after he moved from Houston, Texas, to Notting Hill Gate in London in January that year, jurors heard.

In October 2025, Krom sent several messages to Quietus saying he was planning to turn up at BBC Radio 2 studios in Maida Vale, north London, to meet Ms Hynde whom he believed was giving a live performance there, the court was told.

Even though the performance was actually pre-recorded, and it is not known whether Krom in fact went to the studio, this incident was deemed 'particularly worrying', Mr Ward-Jackson said.

Agency staff decided to report matters to the police and Krom was arrested in May 2026.

He was charged with aggravated stalking.

Judge Christopher Hehir explained to jurors that Krom, who is not present for the trial, is 'seriously mentally ill' and that they will not return a verdict in the traditional sense but a finding on whether or not he did the acts alleged or not.

Ms Hynde is best known for founding rock band Pretenders in 1978 and is the lead vocalist, guitarist and primary songwriter of the chart-topping group.

The group are famed for hits such as Brass In Pocket, Talk Of The Town and Don't Get Me Wrong, and have achieved multiple Grammy nominations, one UK number one single and a chart-topping album.

The trial continues.
